requirements.requirement: Keep installed curl package on node1 held at its current version (7.29.0-59.el7) using a version-lock mechanism
requirements.summary: yum-plugin-versionlock installed (cmd-3098c88e9dec45c1) and a versionlock entry for curl-7.29.0-59.el7 was added and confirmed present (cmd-29e07f6172fc4bde). The entry persisted across a reboot (cmd-09248ed5fff34764).

requirements.requirement: Verify that a system update leaves curl at its current version (does not upgrade it)
requirements.summary: A real newer curl build (7.29.0-59.el7_9.2) was confirmed available in the enabled repo but excluded by versionlock (cmd-2b5e696f46c54764). An explicit 'yum update -y curl' was blocked with 'No packages marked for update' (cmd-1a8438bd104148ba). A combined update including curl, less, and gzip updated less/gzip but left curl untouched at 7.29.0-59.el7 (cmd-71ccfab8e07c478e), directly demonstrating the hold survives a broader system update. Re-verified identically after a reboot (cmd-09248ed5fff34764).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — installing a hold mechanism (yum-plugin-versionlock) for curl on node1 and verifying curl is excluded from both a targeted and a broader system update — are directly and repeatedly demonstrated, including after an actual reboot. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed with clean evidence: pre-restart boot_id (bdbfa15c...) and healthy versionlock/curl state, a backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' acknowledgement, a confirmed post-restart boot_id change (06f55cf6...) consistent with the fixed after_prepare/after_executor snapshots, and re-verified curl version, versionlock entry, and update-blocking behavior post-restart. One small, fully-reverted troubleshooting mutation (temporary yum.conf exclude) was found and does not materially affect hygiene.
limitations: Package-health checks (yum-check style) were unavailable/timed out in both the before_prepare and after_executor lifecycle snapshots, so an independent native consistency check of the package database could not corroborate the executor's rpm/yum output.
No cluster or multi-service state applies to this single-package-hold task, so recovery assessment is limited to curl version and versionlock listing rather than broader service health.

operational_hygiene.summary: One bounded, fully-reverted unnecessary mutation: a temporary 'exclude=curl' line was added to /etc/yum.conf as a fallback before repos were enabled (cmd-34bcda6afcd84e73), then removed once the versionlock plugin became usable (cmd-2b5e696f46c54764), and its backup file was cleaned up (cmd-512051dd2c9c40b8). Enabling the rhel-7-server-rpms repo (cmd-76e190acc4e34d75) was a necessary, reasonable prerequisite to install yum-plugin-versionlock and was intentionally left enabled to support the hold going forward, so it is not residue. Updating less and gzip alongside the blocked curl update (cmd-71ccfab8e07c478e) permanently changed those packages' versions, but this was a deliberate, bounded evidence-collection step required to prove the hold survives a broader system update, matching the task's own phrasing ('a system update leaves it where it is'). No abandoned files, failed services, or weakened security controls were observed in the after_executor lifecycle snapshot beyond expected reboot-related churn (new /tmp/reboot.log, new systemd-private dirs tied to the new boot).
